newsitem.title: FRANCE: Swiss businessman Gaon in French corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Swiss businessman Gaon in French corruption probe.

text.p: A French judge placed billionaire Swiss businessman Nessim Gaon under investigation on Tuesday on suspicion of ordering payment of a 1.45 million franc ($290,000) bribe to the mayor of Cannes, justice sources said.
Gaon is suspected of bribing mayor Michel Mouillot for a permit to put 100 extra slot machines in the Grand Riviera Casino in his Noga-Hilton hotel in the Riviera resort.
Gaon, 76, who is father-in-law of Joel Herzog, son of former Israeli president Haim Herzog, was released on bail after questioning by investigating magistrate Jean-Pierre Murciano.
He was placed under investigation for alleged bribery and misuse of corporate funds.
Mouillot is in custody, as is Herzog, a director of Gaon's Noga group, who was placed under investigation last December for being a suspected accomplice to corruption.
Justice sources said Gaon told the judge that Mouillot had demanded 500,000 francs ($100,000) as a down-payment for the permit. He blamed his son-in-law for paying the bribe.
The Supreme Court last week upheld an appeals court ruling giving Mouillot an 18-month suspended prison sentence for receiving misused corporate funds in a separate political sleaze case.

The mayor, who was declared ineligible to hold public office as a result of that ruling, is also awaiting trial in another case in which he is accused of having solicited bribes from another Cannes casino owned by a British gambling firm.
